items.prompt: A card is drawn at random from a standard 52-card deck. Event A: the card is a heart. Event B: the card is a king. Are A and B independent? There are 13 hearts and 4 kings; one card is the king of hearts.

choices.A: No, because P(A and B) < P(A) x P(B)
choices.B: No, because P(A and B) > P(A) x P(B)
choices.C: Yes, because A and B are mutually exclusive
choices.D: Yes, because P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B)

items.prompt: A bag contains 4 red marbles, 3 blue marbles, and 3 green marbles. One marble is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is blue?
A spinner has 8 equally sized sectors numbered 1 through 8. What is the probability of landing on a number that is either a multiple of 3 or greater than 6?
A standard six-sided die (faces 1–6) is rolled once. Given that the result is even, what is the probability that it is greater than 2?
A game pays $5 if a fair coin lands heads and $0 if it lands tails. What is the expected value of one play?
A lottery ticket wins $100 with probability 0.02, wins $10 with probability 0.10, and wins $0 otherwise. What is the expected winnings per ticket?
A box holds 5 defective and 15 non-defective items. Two items are drawn one at a time without replacement. What is the probability that both are defective?
